title: What America’s Adversaries and Allies Hope to Gain at the U.N. General Assembly
gist: An expert round-up (largely truncated behind a membership wall) arguing that the 2026 U.N. General Assembly opens against a backdrop in which Washington has signalled it no longer intends to sustain the U.N. and the international order it underpins — and that Iran, by contrast, still sees multilateral institutions as useful and will pitch a multipolar, anti-'imperialism' message to the Global South.

themes.theme: U.S. Withdrawal from the Order It Built

insights.claim: The Trump administration has criticized the United Nations, withdrawn from multiple U.N. organizations and reduced funding, which together signal that the United States no longer intends to play its traditional role in sustaining the U.N. and the international political and economic system it underpins.
insights.speaker: Holly Dagres, Raymond Kuo, Nicholas Lokker, Richard Gowan, and Jenny Town
insights.so_what: A structural, not cyclical, withdrawal from multilateral underwriting raises the cost of capital for globally-exposed assets and shifts security provisioning onto regional blocs and middle powers.
insights.quote: have signaled to the world that the United States no longer intends to play its traditional role in sustaining the United Nations and the international political and economic system it underpins
insights.locator: This year’s U.N. General Assembly officially opened

insights.claim: Three distinct U.S. policy moves — withdrawing some troops, shifting security burden onto allies, and imposing tariffs on allies and adversaries alike — are read by outside observers as a single coherent signal of American retrenchment rather than as separate policies.
insights.speaker: Holly Dagres, Raymond Kuo, Nicholas Lokker, Richard Gowan, and Jenny Town
insights.so_what: If tariffs and troop withdrawals are one signal, allied defense spending and de-dollarization hedges should be modeled as correlated responses, not independent policy reactions.
insights.quote: the Trump administration’s moves to withdraw some U.S. troops, shift more of the security burden to allies, and impose tariffs on allies and adversaries alike
insights.locator: U.S. President Donald Trump and his senior officials

insights.claim: Unlike the Trump administration, Tehran still believes in the utility of multilateral institutions like the United Nations, even though it has been unable to use that venue to end the war it is fighting.
insights.speaker: Holly Dagres, Raymond Kuo, Nicholas Lokker, Richard Gowan, and Jenny Town
insights.so_what: Role reversal on multilateralism — a sanctioned adversary defending the institutions Washington is exiting — is a marker of shifting diplomatic legitimacy that matters for future sanctions-coalition durability.
insights.quote: Tehran still believes in the utility of multilateral institutions like the United Nations, though it has been unable to use that venue to bring an end to the war
insights.locator: Holly Dagres Senior Fellow at the Washington Institute

insights.claim: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian is expected to pitch the Global South on a multipolar world and the decline of American 'imperialism' while emphasizing Iranian resilience against the United States and Israel, which launched two wars in the midst of negotiations with Tehran.
insights.speaker: Holly Dagres, Raymond Kuo, Nicholas Lokker, Richard Gowan, and Jenny Town
insights.so_what: Iran is competing for Global South alignment rather than sanctions relief at the U.N. — watch for non-aligned bloc voting shifts that would erode multilateral enforcement of sanctions regimes.
insights.quote: which launched two wars in the midst of negotiations with Tehran
insights.locator: Holly Dagres Senior Fellow at the Washington Institute

insights.claim: The 2026 U.N. General Assembly opened Tuesday, Sept. 8, with most heads of state arriving later in the month for the General Debate beginning Sept. 22 and the session wrapping Sept. 28.
insights.speaker: Holly Dagres, Raymond Kuo, Nicholas Lokker, Richard Gowan, and Jenny Town
insights.so_what: Sept 22-28 is the concentrated window for headline geopolitical risk events and sideline diplomacy — a defined date range for event-driven positioning.
insights.quote: Most heads of state will arrive later this month for the General Debate that begins on Sept. 22. The General Assembly will wrap up on Sept. 28.
insights.locator: This year’s U.N. General Assembly officially opened on Tuesday, Sept. 8

source_meta.author: Holly Dagres, Raymond Kuo, Nicholas Lokker, Richard Gowan, and Jenny Town
